label: For every content type, predicate and negation operator: an expressive predicate does not…
paraphrase: For every content type, predicate and negation operator: an expressive predicate does not collapse; each pole collapses; a collapsed predicate with a decided pivot is at a pole, and the poles exclude each other on inhabited contents; collapse with exclusive negation gives all-fail, with exhaustive negation all-hold, and with both is impossible on inhabited contents. For every truth semantics: no absolute truth entails that the absolute predicate collapses and is not expressive, and on inhabited contents that negation is not exhaustive for it; a thesis that disquotes and captures entails that the global denial fails; total nihilism entails that no assertion commitment in any sense is met and that no agent's predicate is expressive. Conditional laws: they do not say that any rival accepts a hypothesis.
